title: The LPG Reforms of 1991: Liberalisation, Privatisation, and Globalisation

questions.question: At the trough of the 1991 crisis, India's foreign exchange reserves stood at about:
questions.rationale: Reserves fell to roughly US$1.2 billion in mid-1991 — barely two to three weeks of imports — which is why gold was airlifted abroad as collateral.

questions.question: During the 1991 crisis, India pledged about 67 tonnes of gold mainly to:
options: The Union Bank of Switzerland and the Bank of England
The Federal Reserve Bank of New York
questions.rationale: About 20 tonnes went to the Union Bank of Switzerland and about 47 tonnes to the Bank of England, raising roughly US$400 million for debt service.

questions.question: The New Economic Policy was announced on:
questions.rationale: The Industrial Policy Statement of 24 July 1991, under PM Narasimha Rao and FM Manmohan Singh, launched the LPG package after the IMF stand-by arrangement.

questions.question: The 1991 industrial delicensing exempted licensing for all industries except:
questions.rationale: Licensing was abolished for all but 18 industries, a list later cut to 15 and then 9; today only a handful of strategic lines still require licences.

questions.question: The twin rupee devaluations of 1 and 3 July 1991 amounted to a combined depreciation of roughly:
questions.rationale: About 9% on 1 July plus about 11% on 3 July compounded to roughly 18-19%, because the second step applied to the already-devalued rate. (The 36.5% devaluation was in June 1966.)

questions.question: The rupee became convertible on the current account in:
questions.rationale: India accepted IMF Article VIII obligations in August 1994 for current-account convertibility; capital-account convertibility was deliberately withheld after the Tarapore Committee's advice.

questions.question: Which sequence of reform milestones is chronologically correct?
options: WTO membership 1995 — SEBI Act 1992 — current account convertibility 1994
SEBI Act 1992 — current account convertibility 1994 — WTO membership 1995
Current account convertibility 1994 — SEBI Act 1992 — WTO 1995
questions.rationale: SEBI's statutory Act came in 1992, the NSE followed in 1994 along with current-account convertibility, and India signed the WTO agreement in 1994 with effect from 1995.

questions.question: The Narasimham Committee (1991) is associated with reform of:
questions.rationale: It recommended lowering pre-emptions — CRR fell from about 15% to single digits, SLR from 38.5% to 25% — plus interest-rate deregulation; tax reform was the Chelliah Committee's brief.

questions.question: Disinvestment in India began in 1991-92 with the sale of:
options: Minority stakes of about 8-10% in about 40 PSUs
Only loss-making PSUs to workers' cooperatives
questions.rationale: The first phase diluted 8-10% of equity in about 40 PSUs to institutions, raising roughly ₹3,000 crore over two years, without transferring management control.

questions.question: On the Tendulkar poverty line, India's poverty ratio fell from about 45% in 1993-94 to:
questions.rationale: The Tendulkar estimates show poverty at roughly 45% (1993-94) and 22% (2011-12) — the sharpest decline in Indian history, coinciding with post-reform growth.
